SMTO-WEB-0031 — The cited source does not establish what the answer says

GUID: c2634f57-06be-5354-aee6-47103e509470
Slug: research-citation-support-mismatch
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • A statement in the answer has a source attached, but that source doesn't say the same thing. SMTO won't show a citation that doesn't back up its statement.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the run to finish. SMTO sends the answer back to the Model and asks it to match each statement to what its source says. The check compares every statement with its cited source and found one that doesn't agree.
  2. If the run stops, ask SMTO to quote or restate only what the sources say, without adding its own conclusions. Statements that stick to the source's wording pass the check.
  3. If the run stops and an unchecked answer is acceptable to you, open the Research proof validation card shown in the run and turn off Enforce this check for this run. The answer is then shown even though a citation may not support its statement.

What success looks like

  • Each statement in the answer matches what its linked source says.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't accept a citation that only mentions the topic as proof of a specific statement.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Research proof found that the cited evidence does not establish the displayed claim: facts span multiple subjects, a span's subject, predicate or value differs from its fact, claim evidence or source IDs are not among the facts' support, or the claim text differs from the rendered fact wording.

What this means

  • Proof finds mismatched subjects, predicates, values, source membership or displayed claim text across selected facts and their citations. This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.

Why this can happen

  • Proof finds mismatched subjects, predicates, values, source membership or displayed claim text across selected facts and their citations.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare claim text and all fact/span subject, predicate, value and source references.

How to fix it

  • Raised as research_citation_support_mismatch from selected_facts, _verify_fact or _validate_answer (details include claim_id, fact_id, evidence_id or expected_text). Make claim text equal the rendered fact wording (or omit text), cite only evidence and source IDs belonging to the selected same-subject facts, and do not attach a topically related citation to unsupported wording.
  • Correct the claim or citation to match the retained fact; do not attach an unrelated citation to unsupported wording.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • The displayed claim is reproduced by its eligible same-subject evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not attach a citation that merely mentions the topic without establishing the claim.

Technical notes

  • This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
